title: Multiple animations cycles: Survey, Walk, Run -- five frames across its own declared span

criterion.says: Multiple animations cycles: Survey, Walk, Run.

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over a subject that MOVES, so the comparison is taken at every frame of the declared grid rather than at one pose. Nothing here is analytic: what is compared is which pixels each side covers at each sampled time and what colour each body wears there.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: Fox
subjects.notes: Attributes JOINTS_0, POSITION, TEXCOORD_0, WEIGHTS_0. 3 animations over a declared span of 3.41667 s, and 1 skin. The file's own images are not read by this case: the material below declares its colours, so what is compared is where the geometry is at each frame and which body wears which row.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [-12.592718124389648, -0.12174476683139801, -88.09500122070312] to [12.592718124389648, 78.90718841552734, 66.62486267089844], so centre = [0.0, 39.39272182434797, -10.735069274902344] and radius = 87.77544468930186 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 626.8610233697558, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject; `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint and never choose it.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. A material a primitive does not name is keyed by `<default>`, which is the format's own word for the material an undefined `material` selects.

fps.note: ONE FRAME PER SECOND, AND THE RATE IS AN INTEGER BECAUSE THE HARNESS REQUIRES ONE: a frame is `index / fps` seconds and Blender's own rate is whole. A rate below one -- which is what sampling a 60 s span in five steps would need -- has no spelling, so the grid is a second apart and the note below says what it therefore covers.

frames.derivation: min(5, ceil(3.41666675 s) + 1) = 5, so the grid runs 0..4 s.
frames.note: WHAT THIS GRID COVERS, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. The file's declared span is 3.41666675 s and this case samples its first 4 s. Where the span is shorter than that, glTF clamps past the last keyframe and the tail frames state the end pose rather than an extrapolation. Where it is LONGER -- and it is for the long ones -- this case exercises the OPENING of the motion and says so: it decides that the animation is read, applied and posed, not that the whole of it is right. A case that needed the whole span would declare a grid for it and pay for the frames.

animation.note: ONE ANIMATION, BECAUSE THE FILE'S ARE ALTERNATIVES AND NOT LAYERS. This asset carries three, and they drive the same node paths -- glTF says only that within ONE animation a target must not be used twice, and leaves two animations on one property undefined. A viewer plays one. Declaring all three asked the poser to apply them at once, which it refuses by name rather than resolving by order, and the case could not run at all. The other two are a case each when someone wants them; this one decides the first.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case over a moving subject. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0, recomputed by the runner on every run and refused on mismatch; seeded from that recomputation, so it pins the framing and detects drift.
